South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 02/07/28 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of persistent lower extremity edema, and mental health support.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax presents for follow-up approximately four weeks after his last visit. He reports that his respiratory symptoms have remained stable since the adjustment of his inhaler regimen. He continues to use albuterol approximately three to four times daily, indicating a reduction in usage compared to the previous visit. Mr. Fairfax notes that while he experiences occasional wheezing, particularly during cold weather, he has not had any nocturnal awakenings due to respiratory distress.
However, he expresses ongoing concern regarding his bilateral lower extremity edema, which has not shown any significant improvement. He continues to adhere strictly to his dietary sodium restrictions and has been compliant with his furosemide regimen. Mr. Fairfax states that he experiences significant discomfort due to the swelling, particularly when standing for prolonged periods.
In terms of his mental health, Mr. Fairfax reports continued benefits from mindfulness practices and states that his anxiety levels have been manageable. He acknowledges some difficulties with sleep, stating that he occasionally wakes up feeling anxious, but overall feels more equipped to handle stressors.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + dyspnea on exertion, + intermittent wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + ongoing joint pain, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using three to four times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 2 puffs twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs daily (increased). 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 120 mg daily (unchanged). 7. Sertraline 100 mg daily.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 78, BP 126/76, RR 22, O2 sat 80% on room air.
General: Elderly male in mild respiratory distress, appears fatigued but engaged. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, mild wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 3+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 9.2, Hgb 10.8, Hct 31.5, Plt 215. 2. BMP: Na 130, K 4.0, Cl 99, CO2 27, BUN 34, Cr 2.0, Glucose 92. 3. BNP: 580 (stable). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 2.6 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax's respiratory symptoms remain stable with the current inhaler regimen. Continue albuterol as needed and maintain the increased tiotropium dose of 2 puffs daily to enhance bronchodilation. A follow-up pulmonary function test is recommended in one month to evaluate lung function and medication efficacy. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The persistent edema remains a concern. Reinforcement of dietary sodium restrictions is crucial. A follow-up with nephrology is advised to reassess renal function and diuretic therapy. Consideration for an increase in furosemide dosage may be warranted based on nephrology recommendations. 4. Mental health: Mr. Fairfax continues to benefit from mindfulness practices. Continue sertraline 100 mg daily. Follow-up with psychiatry in one month for ongoing management and reassessment of treatment efficacy. Further exploration of relaxation techniques is encouraged.
Patient education reiterated regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
